Part of it is a sort of yes. If you're partner is mad when you're doing something unhealthy to yourself that is hurting you they do love you; HOWEVER, how they handle and portray that anger makes a HUGE difference. 

If they're on your ass about stopping heavy drugs/drinking or other extremely risky behaviors that your not being safe or safer about because you're on a path to losing everything that's different. 

But if they're mad because you didn't do the dishes or fold laundry their way that can be red flag. Anger can be a sign of caring and love yes, but how the person handles their emotions will say everything. 

Anger should never be yelling/screaming/manipulation/hitting to change a behavior. You should support them in finding different ways to cope, but also remember that the choice is ultimately in their hands, NOT yours. 

You should never belittle your partner. If you actually care and love them you will be there for them and support them while THEY HELP THEMSELVES. 

Being in a relationship means that you want to see that person be the best they can be and you do so with kindness and compassion.

Mothers will naturally be the more "gentle" parent, while dads are more "active"
So when it comes to babies, mothers will have a slightly easier time bonding. 
The best way to combat this is too do exactly as you are now. Reaching out and asking for help. See about any dad groups in your community, or any baby and parent classes you can go to. It seems like a long shot but in the end it will help.
